sections.overview: This noctuid moth is recorded across parts of southeastern Europe and western Asia.
sections.identification: It belongs to Schinia, in the heliothine subfamily of Noctuidae.
sections.habitat: It is associated with warm, dry places such as steppe, sandy grassland and dry slopes.
sections.diet: The larvae feed on Chondrilla juncea, a plant in the daisy family.
sections.behavior: Adults fly by day, usually from late June to mid-August.
sections.reproduction: Larvae occur on the host plant’s flowers and fruits in late summer.
sections.ecology: A molecular study groups it with S. cardui; both were specialists on the plant tribe Lactuceae in that study.
sections.conservation: The Belgian catalogue treats it as an exotic visitor there and records one specimen from 1909.
